science.title: Vitamin D status and its association with musculoskeletal symptoms and degenerative bone disease among orthopaedic outpatients in Nepal
science.description: The objective of this study was to evaluate the association between vitamin D status and demographic characteristics, musculoskeletal pain, and degenerative bone diseases in Orthopedic outpatients. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 215 patients attending the Orthopaedic Outpatient Department of a hospital in Nepal. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire, and serum vitamin D levels were categorized as deficient (≤ 20 ng/mL), insufficient (21–29 ng/mL), and sufficient (≥ 30 ng/mL). Multiple correspondence analysis (MCA) and ordinal logistic regression analysis were used to examine the distribution and correlates of vitamin D status. The most prevalent category was vitamin D insufficiency (21–29 ng/mL), with 62.3% of participants affected, and 9.8% were vitamin D deficient. Females were less likely to be in the higher vitamin D category than males (AOR = 0.37, 95% CI: 0.18–0.77, p = 0.008), and participants without degenerative bone disease had lower odds of being in a higher vitamin D category (AOR = 0.40, 95% CI: 0.20–0.81, p = 0.010). MCA showed that Body pain was a common symptom among participants with suboptimal vitamin D status. Further longitudinal, multicenter studies are needed to elucidate the association between vitamin D status and degenerative bone disease and symptoms.

science.title: AI automates 3D membrane mapping, matching manual results in a fraction of time
science.description: Cell membranes and the proteins within them control many vital processes and play a key role in health and disease. But studying them in 3D images of cells has so far meant slow, manual work. A team from Helmholtz Munich, the Technical University of Munich (TUM) and the Biozentrum of the University of Basel has developed MemBrain v2, an AI tool that automates this task—cutting work that once took weeks down to a few hours. The study is published in Nature Methods.

science.title: AMCOS-Net: a novel attention-based multimodal fusion architecture for automated corneal opacity segmentation
science.description: Corneal opacity is one of the major causes of visual impairment across the world, and there is no objective way to diagnose it due to the subjectivity involved in the clinical assessment. To address this, the present study offers a multimodal deep learning framework which segments corneal opacity using anterior segment optical coherence tomography and anterior segment photography. This method utilizes the multimodal corneal opacity assessment dataset, which comprises 6664 multimodal images that provide both structural information of the cornea, and surface-level information. A number of segmentation baseline architectures, such as U-Net, U-Net++, Attention U-Net, V-Net, SegNet, and DeepLabV3+, were investigated with the use of early, mid, and late fusion strategies. It was found that mid-fusion level integration yielded the best results. Based on this, an architecture named AMCOS-Net was designed, which integrated dual-encoders, mid-level fusion with attention and atrous spatial pyramid pooling to capture context at multiple scales. AMCOS-Net has shown a small improvement in the quantitative results compared to all baseline models, with a mean segmentation Dice score of 0.584 and a mean intersection over union score of 0.412, and also showed a moderate improvement in the localization and segmentation of the corneal opacity boundaries. All of the above results could be considered as a preliminary study which has the potential for a multimodal fusion of two modalities that provide different pathological information about the cornea.
